A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OpenNER 1.0 and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding material can be matched despite reflow, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original encoder fine-tuning and LLM evaluation results across the collection, plus prompting trials in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds statistical comparisons and a reported post-hoc XLM-R Large evaluation.

M1.justification: The standardization pipeline, label repairs, entity mappings, encoder classification procedure, and five-shot LLM approach remain unchanged. The added XLM-R Large comparison is a baseline evaluation, not a revised proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 36 corpora, 52 languages, and 67 dataset-language combinations, with full and core ontologies. The CoNLL-03 prompting trials also appear in both appendices. Added Glot500 pretraining-language information documents existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds an explicitly reported post-hoc comparison of XLM-R Large against Base in Section 4, footnote 3. The main comparisons retain mBERT, XLM-R Base, Glot500, Aya-Expanse 32b, and QwQ-32B-Preview.

E3.justification: The added XLM-R Large evaluation introduces a larger model configuration, although its detailed protocol is unspecified. Existing dataset splits, scoring, fine-tuning hyperparameters, and multilingual training cap remain unchanged. The newly specified MasakhaNER commit does not establish a change to the data previously used.

E4.justification: v3 adds a limited model-size sensitivity check, reporting that XLM-R Large performs worse than Base. The appendix comparisons of JSON, inline, and five-shot prompting, and the dataset annotation-error analyses, remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 adds an inferential layer to the main core-type comparisons: pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across 67 dataset-language combinations, separately for individual and multilingual models, with Bonferroni correction and p-values. It also newly reports aggregate standard errors for full-ontology results. The ten fine-tuning seeds and three LLM seeds remain unchanged; existing core-type aggregate uncertainties move into appendix mean rows.

E6.justification: Matched per-dataset scores and standard errors in v2 Tables 5, 6, and 12 are retained in v3 Tables 6, 7, and 8. New findings include significance outcomes and XLM-R Large underperforming Base. However, Section 4.2 reports individual-model gaps of 0.44 and 6.97 F1 where Table 4 implies 1.00 and 6.41, respectively.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations. The added description of standard Wilcoxon testing and Bonferroni correction concerns statistical procedures rather than a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a standardized multilingual, multi-ontology NER collection with baseline evaluations. Both versions claim that no model is best across all languages and that the evaluated LLM approaches lag behind. Rewording the largest-collection claim and replacing the contribution list do not materially change this scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets multilingual model differences as statistically reliable while qualifying the individual XLM-R versus Glot500 difference as nonsignificant. It clarifies their contrasting individual versus multilingual performance and adds a tuning caveat for XLM-R Large. Existing coverage, script, and annotation-consistency limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 promises a future release; v3 documents release through a concrete repository, assembly/preprocessing code, hosting directions, and collection-versus-dataset licensing terms. This substantially changes documented resource access. Appendix A.1 also specifies the MasakhaNER commit and its rationale, while Table 9 adds Glot500 pretraining-language coverage.

R1.justification: Positioning relative to UNER, automatically annotated resources, and existing NER approaches remains stable. The removed GPT-NER 2023 preprint duplicates the 2025 published work already cited in v2 and retained in v3; it is not a removed research comparison.

P1.justification: v3 replaces the introductory contribution list with an explanation of the two resource versions, refines wording and appendix examples, updates author contact information, and adds acknowledgments. The principal section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 5, a violin visualization of existing scores; moves core-type counts into the main text; groups the LLM results with other appendix results; and adds table mean rows and a Glot500 language-information column. The pipeline figure and Figures 2–4 are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves practical usability through concrete release, licensing, and data-version documentation, and adds statistical comparisons and clearer result summaries. These gains are moderated by the new Section 4.2 F1-gap inconsistencies with Table 4 and the sparse documentation of XLM-R Large. Overall, the revision provides a modest net improvement.
